_comment: Palo Alto Cortex XDR -- Behavioral IOC (BIOC) Prevention Rules
Each rule below uses Cortex XQL with `behavior: PREVENTION` to
block. Set `behavior: DETECTION` initially for tuning.
Generic: matches every legitimate disk tool, gets exempted.
HARDENED v2 (below): conjunction of (disk-class kernel path) AND
(actor not Microsoft-signed) AND (actor in user path)

rules.name: Petya-Class: Raw-disk write by untrusted actor
rules.query: dataset = xdr_data | filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_OPEN_FOR_WRITE) and (action_file_path ~= "^\\\\Device\\\\Harddisk" or action_file_path ~= "^\\\\\\?\\\\PhysicalDrive" or action_file_path ~= "^\\\\\\.\\\\PhysicalDrive" or action_file_path ~= "^\\\\\\.\\\\Volume\\{") and actor_effective_thumbprint = null and (actor_process_image_path ~= "\\\\Users\\\\" or actor_process_image_path ~= "\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\" or actor_process_image_path ~= "\\\\ProgramData\\\\" or actor_process_image_path ~= "\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\") and actor_process_image_name not in ("defrag.exe","chkdsk.exe","diskpart.exe","fsutil.exe","vds.exe","vdsldr.exe","vssvc.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","drvinst.exe","smartctl.exe","WerFault.exe")
_tightening_notes: 1. file event is a write-intent open
2. target path resolves to a kernel disk-class object
(covers all Win32 syntaxes -- the kernel canonicalises)
4. actor process lives in a user-writable directory
5. actor process image name is not a known disk-tool
An attacker has to defeat ALL five to evade. The most
achievable defeat is signing the binary -- which moves
the cost from 'free recompile' to 'acquire EV cert or
compromise a vendor cert', a materially harder ask.

rules.name: Petya-Class: Dropper CLI fingerprint
rules.query: dataset = xdr_data | filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_command_line ~= "(--install|--write-stage2|--backup-mbr|--restore-mbr|--bsod)" and action_process_image_command_line ~= "(--drive|PhysicalDrive|Device\\\\Harddisk|stage2\\.bin|mbr\\.bin)" and actor_process_image_name in ("explorer.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wmiprvse.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","firefox.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","outlook.exe")
_tightening_notes: Requires 2 independent CLI vocabularies AND an interactive
ancestor. A single CLI atom by itself (e.g., the word
'PhysicalDrive' in a log file) does not fire.

rules.name: Petya-Class: Known artifact filenames
rules.query: dataset = xdr_data | filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_RENAME) and action_file_name in ("OpenPetya.exe","stage2.bin","mbr.bin") and not action_file_path contains "\\Backup\\" and not action_file_path contains "\\Quarantine\\" and not action_file_path contains "\\EDR-Sandbox\\"
_tightening_notes: Filename-based. Cheap. Defeated by rename. Pair with the
two rules above for real coverage.
